# HerraduraKEx

> Cryptographic suite implementing classical, NL/PQC, and code-based-PQC protocols
> on the FSCX (Full Surroundings Cyclic XOR) primitive and GF(2^n)* Diffie-Hellman
> arithmetic. Implementations in C, Go, Python, ARM Thumb-2 asm, NASM i386 asm, Arduino.
> This file is a condensed, agent/tool-facing API index. It is generated from and must
> stay consistent with CLAUDE.md (build/test/architecture) and docs/TUTORIAL.md
> (worked examples) — those are the authoritative documents for anything not covered
> here. Do not treat this file as authoritative for build commands or protocol math;
> see README.md and SecurityProofs-{1..7}.md for the formal definitions.

## Authoritative docs (read these for detail, not this file)
- CLAUDE.md — repo layout, build/test commands, protocol stack overview
- README.md — protocol descriptions with math (KaTeX)
- docs/TUTORIAL.md — API usage guide per protocol and language, with worked examples
- docs/INTRODUCTION.md — lay-audience primer
- SecurityProofs.md (+ -1 through -7.md) — formal security analysis
- BITARRAY.md — the NORMATIVE BitArray specification (TODO #314).  One variable-width
  bit-string type, big-endian octets with the width carried WITH the value, replacing the
  embedded bignum types.  ALL FOUR PORTS CONFORM — C since v9.1.0, Go v9.2.0, Python
  v9.3.0, Java v9.4.0.  Read
  §3 before touching width-taking code: a binary operation REQUIRES equal widths and a
  mismatch is E_MIXED_WIDTH, never a coercion
- docs/examples/{python,c,go}/hello_herradura.* — minimal integration samples

## Protocol identifiers (used as --algo values across all four CLIs; also the naming
## convention for functions in every language binding)
Key exchange:     hkex-gf, hkex-rnl, hybrid-rnl-stern
Symmetric enc:    hske, hske-nla1, hske-nla2, hske-nla3, hske-duplex, hske-duplex3
Asymmetric enc:   hpke, hpke-nl, hpke-nl3, hpke-stern, hpke-stern-kem
Signatures:       hpks, hpks-nl, hpks-stern, hpks-ring, hpks-wots, hpks-xmss,
                  hpks-zkp-nl (genpkey) / nl-zkboo, nl-zkbpp (sign/verify), rnl-sigma,
                  hpks-t (threshold, via threshold-* subcommands)
Other primitives: oprf (OPRF/aPAKE), hcred (anonymous credentials), hfscx-256,
                  hfscx-256-ds (digest), fpe, twk (256-bit tweakable block enc; fpe is
                  NOT FF1/FF3-1 format-preserving despite the name — see SECURITY.md),
                  rand (HDRBG)
NL-FSCX v3 (TODO #255): the -nla3 / -duplex3 / -nl3 tags above, plus `fpe --v3` and
                  `twk --v3`, run the chi-hardened round at R3_VALUE=160 instead of
                  v2's 192.  All five are ADDED alongside their v2 counterparts, not
                  replacements: no stored artifact changes, and the two versions do
                  not interoperate.  fpe/twk take a flag rather than new subcommands
                  because both are already reached by subcommand rather than by tag.
                  There is deliberately NO key check on any v3 path.  Ratings differ
                  per tag (SECURITY.md): hske-nla3 and twk --v3 are production-track
                  (conjectured) since TODO #345, like hske-nla2 and twk, and are the
                  ones to prefer; hske-duplex3 is research, hpke-nl3 demo-only, and
                  fpe --v3 broken as named.

Not every identifier is valid for every subcommand — see the CLI section below for the
exact choices list per subcommand.

## Core protocol summaries
- HKEX-GF: classical DH over GF(2^n)*, generator g=3. pub = g^priv; shared = their_pub^priv.
- HKEX-RNL: Ring-LWR key exchange. Two-round: responder (Bob) replies to
  initiator's (Alice's) public key first; Alice completes using Bob's response PEM.
  Ring dimension n=1024 since v2.7.19 (~206 classical / ~187 quantum Core-SVP bits).
  Keys from before v2.7.19 used n=256 and are worth only ~32 bits — regenerate them.
  The ring dimension is separate from the 256-bit derived session key.
- HSKE / HSKE-NLA1 / HSKE-NLA2 / HSKE-duplex: symmetric encryption via
  FSCX_REVOLVE(plaintext, key, i) forward / FSCX_REVOLVE(ciphertext, key, r) inverse
  (r = n - i mod period); NL variants use NL-FSCX v1 (counter-mode keystream) or v2
  (invertible revolve) primitives instead of classical FSCX, and add AEAD framing.
- HPKS / HPKS-NL: Schnorr-style signature over GF(2^n)*, challenge hashed via
  (NL-)FSCX_REVOLVE of the commitment and message.
- HPKE / HPKE-NL: El Gamal-style encryption; shared enc/dec key derived via DH, payload
  encrypted with (NL-)FSCX_REVOLVE.
- HPKS-Stern-F / HPKE-Stern(-KEM): Stern zero-knowledge identification protocol
  (code-based, syndrome decoding) turned into a Fiat-Shamir signature / Niederreiter KEM.
  N = 256 by default (~2^24, demo); N = 2304 is the 128-bit set (--level 128), the "long
  form": N-bit values as byte strings, 256-bit commitments and message (SPEC.md §11.1).
- HPKS-ring: ring signature built on HPKS-Stern-F.
- rnl-sigma / nl-zkboo / nl-zkbpp: Sigma-protocol and ZKBoo/ZKB++ MPC-in-the-head proofs
  over Ring-LWR / NL-FSCX statements.
- HPKS-t: threshold Schnorr signature (4-phase protocol: commit, aggregate, respond,
  combine — see threshold-* CLI subcommands).
- HPKS-WOTS / HPKS-XMSS: hash-based one-time / stateful many-time signatures.
  Demo-only since TODO #346, with HFSCX-256 (zero proven margin on its compression
  function); HSKE-NL-A1 is production-track only under a 2^64-block per-key limit.
- OPRF / aPAKE (HPAKE): 2HashDH oblivious PRF, used to build an augmented PAKE.
- HCRED: anonymous credentials (Stern-F signature issuance + ZKBoo presentation proof).
- FPE / TWK: format-preserving and tweakable-wide-block encryption of a single 256-bit
  block, keyed by a session key.
- HDRBG (rand): deterministic byte generator seeded from entropy, with checkpointable
  state PEMs.
- HAccum: Merkle-style cryptographic accumulator (leaf/node/root/prove/verify).
- Ratchet: simple forward-secret key ratchet (init/advance).
- QC-MDPC: KEM keygen/encap/BGF-decode primitives (production needs a full decoder).

## herradura.h — C header-only library
Single-include; all exported symbols prefixed ba_, gf_, nl_, rnl_, hkex_, hske_,
hpks_, hpke_, stern_, hpks_stern_/hpke_stern_, zkp_, hcred_, hpkst_, oprf_, hpake_,
drbg_, haccum_, ratchet_, fpe_, twk_, qcmdpc_. Key public entry points:

  void hkex_gf_pubkey(const BitArray *priv, BitArray *pub);
  int  hkex_gf_agree(const BitArray *priv, const BitArray *their_pub, BitArray *shared);
  void hske_encrypt(const BitArray *pt, const BitArray *key, BitArray *ct);
  void hske_decrypt(const BitArray *ct, const BitArray *key, BitArray *pt);
  void hpks_sign(const BitArray *msg, const BitArray *priv, BitArray *R, BitArray *s, FILE *urnd);
  void hpks_nl_sign(const BitArray *msg, const BitArray *priv, BitArray *R, BitArray *s, FILE *urnd);  /* #308 */
  int  hpks_verify(const BitArray *msg, const BitArray *pub, const BitArray *R, const BitArray *s);
  int  hpke_encrypt(const BitArray *pt, const BitArray *pub, BitArray *R, BitArray *ct, FILE *urnd);
  int  hpke_decrypt(const BitArray *ct, const BitArray *R, const BitArray *priv, BitArray *pt);
  void hske_nl_aead_encrypt(...); int hske_nl_aead_decrypt(...);
  void hske_nl_v2_duplex_encrypt(...); int hske_nl_v2_duplex_decrypt(...);
  void hske_nl_v3_duplex_encrypt(...); int hske_nl_v3_duplex_decrypt(...);   /* #255 */
  void nl_fscx_revolve_v3_ba(...);     void nl_fscx_revolve_v3_inv_ba(...);
  void fpe_v3_encrypt/decrypt(...);    void twk_v3_encrypt/decrypt(...);
  void hpks_stern_f_sign(SternSig *sig, ...); int hpks_stern_f_verify(const SternSig *sig, ...);
  void hpke_stern_f_encap(...); void hpke_stern_f_decap_known(...);
  void stern_l_keygen(...); void hpks_stern_l_sign(SternLSig *sig, ...);   /* N = 2304, #382 */
  int hpks_stern_l_verify(...); void stern_l_ring_sign/verify(...); void hpke_stern_l_encap(...);
  void hpks_wots_keygen/sign/verify(...); void hpks_xmss_keygen/sign/verify(...);

Read herradura.h directly for full signatures of NL-FSCX, Ring-LWR (rnl_*), Stern-ring,
ZKP-NL, HCRED, HPKST, OPRF/HPAKE, FPE/TWK, HDRBG, HAccum, ratchet, and QC-MDPC —
grep the prefixes above.

## Go — package herradura (herradura/herradura.go, herradura/codec.go)
Import path: herradurakex/herradura (module herradurakex; see go.mod / replace directives
for HerraduraCli). NOTE: the root "Herradura cryptographic suite.go" is `package main`
(CLI demo only) — the reusable library lives under herradura/.

Representative exported names (CamelCase mirrors the C/Python snake_case identifiers,
e.g. hkex_gf_agree -> corresponding Go call in the kex flow):
  Fscx, FscxRevolve, GfMul, GfPow, NewBitArray, NewRandBitArray, NewFromBytes
  NlFscxV1/V2/V2Inv, NlFscxRevolveV1/V2/V2Inv
  Hfscx256, Hfscx256DS, HmacHfscx256
  RnlKeygen, RnlAgree, RnlHint, RnlReconcileBits
  SternFKeygen, HpksSternFSign/Verify, HpkeSternFEncap/DecapKnown, HpksSternRingSign/Verify
  SternLKeygen, HpksSternLSign/Verify, HpksSternLRingSign/Verify, HpkeSternLEncap  (N = 2304)
  RnlSigmaSign/Verify, ZkpNlKeygen/Prove/Verify
  HpksWotsKeygen/Sign/Verify, HpksXmssKeygen/Sign/Verify
  HcredUserKeygen/Prove/Verify, HcredIssue/CredVerify
  HpkstAggregatePublickeys/Sign/Verify
  OprfKeygen/Blind/Eval/Unblind/Direct, HpakeRegister/LoginDemo
  FpeEncrypt/Decrypt, TwkEncrypt/Decrypt, DrbgSeed/FromState
  HaccumLeaf/Node/Root/Prove/Verify, RatchetInit/Advance
  PemWrap/Unwrap, DerIntEnc/SeqEnc, DerParseSeq (codec.go)

## Python — "Herradura cryptographic suite.py"
Filename contains spaces: load via importlib (see docs/examples/python/hello_herradura.py
and HerraduraCli/primitives.py for the exact pattern). Function names are snake_case and
match the C API 1:1 (fscx, fscx_revolve, gf_mul, gf_pow, nl_fscx_v1/v2/v2_inv,
hfscx_256, hfscx_256_ds, hmac_hfscx_256, stern_f_keygen, hpks_stern_f_sign/verify,
hpke_stern_f_encap/decap, hcred_*, hpkst_*, oprf_*, hpake_*, fpe_encrypt/decrypt,
twk_encrypt/decrypt, fpe_v3_*/twk_v3_*, nl_fscx_*_v3, haccum_*, ratchet_init/advance,
qcmdpc_*). BitArray is the core
class (BitArray.random(n)). Notable constants: KEYBITS, GF_POLY, GF_GEN, I_VALUE,
R_VALUE.

## HerraduraCli — OpenSSL-style CLI (herradura.py / herradura_cli.c / herradura_cli_go / Java herradurakex.HerraduraCli)
All four implementations share one PEM wire format and subcommand interface;
PEM files from any one are byte-for-byte readable by the others.  Per-CLI support
for every --algo tag and flag is in spec/herradura-protocol-spec.json
(cli_support, cli_flag_matrix); deliberate per-CLI differences are in its
cli_surface_gaps.
Every key flag is checked against that file's key_label_acceptance table: a key of
the wrong type fails with "wrong key type: <flag> holds '<label>'; accepted: ...".
The GF keys (hkex-gf, hpks, hpks-nl, hpke, hpke-nl) are interchangeable, as are
hpks-stern and hpke-stern; every other key serves only its own --algo, and a
--pubkey / --their / --ring / --issuer slot takes public keys only (HCRED's
cred-verify --pubkey and cred-issue --in also take the HCRED private key).
A DER-SEQUENCE PEM with the wrong number of items fails with "malformed PEM
'<label>': <k> DER items, expected <n>" (pem_der_items in the same file), and an
out-of-range width, ring dimension or field size fails with a one-line bound error.
A peer GF value (public key, ciphertext R) of 0 or 1, or an HKEX-RNL peer C that is
zero, sparse or clustered, is refused as a degenerate key.  GF keys, and hpks-stern /
hpke-stern keys (hpks-ring too), run at 32/64/128/256 bits in the Python, C and Go CLIs
(C since TODO #383 stages 1 and 2) and at 256 only in Java, which
refuses any other declared width ("n is 128 (this CLI runs n = 256)").  A key used with a
peer key, ciphertext or signature of another width fails ("kex: their public key n is
128, our private key n is 64").  Each artifact has one encoding:
bytes after a DER SEQUENCE, a raw-body PEM's last field or an .hkx tag are refused, a
field wider than its writer pads it to fails with "<label>: field <i> is <k> bytes
(expected at most <cap>)" (pem_der_field_caps), and an HPKS signature whose stored
challenge e is not the recomputed one is refused.  A fixed-width field must be exactly
its width ("is encoded in <k> bytes (expected exactly <w>)"), any other field minimal
("encoded with a leading zero byte"), every DER length in its shortest form, and
HKEX-RNL coefficients and QC-MDPC values in range ("field <i> coefficient <j> is <v>
(expected below <b>)", "has bits at or above r = <r>").

Every numeric flag takes decimal digits only (no sign, space, 0x, _ or exponent) in a
stated range, and anything else fails in all four CLIs with "<cmd>: <flag> must be a
decimal integer from <lo> to <hi>, got '<v>'" (TODO #375, #380): --kdf-iterations
1..100000000, --xmss-height 1..20, rand --bytes 0..33554432 (one seed's worth of DRBG
output), every --rounds and --min-rounds 1..4096 (what every verifier accepts), twk
--sector 0..2^64-1 and --bidx 0..2^32-1.  An explicit value is never read as the
default: sign --rounds 0 is refused, not signed at 219.  (genpkey --bits / --level: below.)

One rule for the shape of a command line, in all four CLIs (TODO #381): --flag=value
is --flag value, and a boolean flag (--aead --decrypt --encrypt --hex --pubout --text
--v3) refuses a value; a value-taking flag at the end of the line, or followed by another
of its subcommand's flags, fails "<cmd>: <flag> needs a value"; a word that is neither a
flag nor a flag's value fails "<cmd>: unexpected argument '<w>'"; --in naming a directory
fails "Is a directory".  A flag Python's argparse requires is required in every CLI (Go
used to default 19 --in/--out flags to stdin/stdout); stdin and stdout are spelled "-".
(Python's own refusals keep argparse's wording.)

  genpkey --algo <ID> [--bits N | --level L] [--xmss-height N] [--passphrase P | --passphrase-file F [--kdf-iterations N]] --out FILE
    <ID> in: hkex-gf, hkex-rnl, hpks, hpks-nl, hpke, hpke-nl, hpke-nl3, hpks-stern,
             hpke-stern, hpke-stern-kem, hpks-zkp-nl, oprf, hpks-xmss, hpks-wots, hcred
    Key sizes come from one table, spec's key_parameter_sets, generated into all four
    CLIs (TODO #379).  --level names the strength a set is sized for: demo, 128 (192 and
    256 reserved); --bits names a row by width (key width, HKEX-RNL ring dimension or
    Stern-F N) and is kept for compatibility.  GF family (hkex-gf hpks hpks-nl hpke
    hpke-nl hpke-nl3) and oprf: --bits 32|64|128|256, --level demo = 256, no --level 128
    (demo-only at every width).  hkex-rnl: 32|64|128|256 (demo), 1024 = --level 128
    (default); 512 refused as withdrawn.  hpks-stern, hpke-stern, hcred: 32|64|128|256,
    --level demo = 256; hpks-stern and hpke-stern also 2304 = --level 128 (TODO #382; hcred
    refuses --level 128, its issuer's hpks-stern key is what takes it).  hpke-stern-kem: --level 128 only.  hpks-zkp-nl: --bits any even
    n <= 64, --level demo = 8.  hpks-wots, hpks-xmss: neither flag.  Below the default a
    stderr warning gives the estimated security.  Every listed width runs in all four
    CLIs (TODO #383, #384, #385).  Anything else fails by name; --bits with --level fails.
    --passphrase writes a HERRADURA ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY envelope.  An empty
    passphrase, and --kdf-iterations without --passphrase, are refused by name in
    every CLI (TODO #376; Python and Go used to write the key in the clear).
    --passphrase-file F reads it from F instead (`-` = stdin), keeping it off the
    command line, where other local users can read it (TODO #396).  The secret is F's
    bytes minus at most one trailing \n or \r\n; more than 1024 bytes, a NUL, another
    CR/LF, invalid UTF-8, or both forms at once are refused by name.  Same rule for
    pkey --passphrase-file and pake-* --password-file.
  pkey --in FILE [--pubout] [--text] [--out FILE]
    --text prints one layout per algorithm, byte-identical in all four CLIs, ending in
    the key's parameter-set row (`level : ...` where it has one, `security : ...`;
    none for WOTS / XMSS).  A PUBLIC key is refused by label (TODO #386, #387).
  pkey --decrypt (--passphrase P | --passphrase-file F) --in FILE [--out FILE]
    --decrypt accepts --passphrase '' so envelopes written under '' before TODO #376
    stay readable.
  kex --algo {hkex-gf,hkex-rnl,hybrid-rnl-stern} --our FILE --their FILE --out FILE
      [--kdf {none,hfscx-256}] [--their-kem FILE] [--our-kem FILE]
    hkex-rnl is two-round: responder replies first, initiator completes with the response PEM.
    hybrid-rnl-stern is hkex-rnl plus a QC-MDPC KEM: the responder passes --their-kem
    (the initiator's hpke-stern-kem public key), the initiator --our-kem (its private key).
    Python's --kdf also accepts sp800227 (hkex-rnl only; spec cli_flag_value_gaps).
    hkex-gf --kdf hfscx-256 at any width n: sk = HFSCX-256(g^ab as n/8 bytes), written
    whole as a SESSION KEY declaring n = 256 (an HSKE key); without --kdf, raw g^ab at n.
  enc/dec --algo {hske,hske-nla1,hske-nla2,hske-nla3,hske-duplex,hske-duplex3,
                  hpke,hpke-nl,hpke-nl3,hpke-stern,hpke-stern-kem}
           --key|--pubkey FILE --in FILE --out FILE [--aead] [--ad STR]
    --aead/--ad apply to hske-nla1 (and both duplex variants are inherently AEAD).
    Every other algo encrypts ONE block (32 bytes; hske-nla1 without --aead, the
    key's width) and refuses longer input with "enc: --algo <a> encrypts one
    <k>-byte block; --in is <l> bytes (...)"; shorter input comes back zero-padded.
    --ad is refused at enc and dec on any algo but hske-duplex, hske-duplex3 and
    hske-nla1, --aead on any but hske-nla1, and dec hske-nla1 --ad on a non-AEAD
    ciphertext; --ad '' counts as given (TODO #378; they used to be dropped).
    hske-nla1 was 256-BIT ONLY from v9.0.0 (TODO #313) to v9.4.0: below 256 the
    four ports produced four different keystreams and, A1 having no
    authentication tag, dec wrote garbage and exited 0.  Since v9.5.0 (TODO #314
    pass 6) the four agree octet for octet and enc/dec accept EVERY legal
    BitArray width -- a multiple of 8 from 16 to 256 (BITARRAY.md 2).  Two
    refusals remain at dec, both about the format: a declared width no BitArray
    can have, and a ciphertext whose declared nbits disagrees with the key's
    (BITARRAY.md 3 -- a mixed width is never coerced).  encfile/decfile stay
    256-bit: the .hkx container has no width field.  See MIGRATING.md 23.
    hske-duplex3 ciphertexts carry format tag 4, hske-duplex's tag 3, so each
    refuses the other's artifact at the parser.  All four CLIs ship both duplex
    versions.
  sign --algo {hpks,hpks-nl,hpks-stern,rnl-sigma,nl-zkboo,nl-zkbpp,hpks-xmss,hpks-wots,hpks-ring}
       --key FILE [--ring FILE1,FILE2,...] --in FILE --out FILE
       [--digest {hfscx-256,none}] [--rounds N]
    --digest defaults to hfscx-256 (TODO #365, v15.0.0): the whole input is
    hashed and the 32-byte digest signed.  none pads/truncates the input to 32
    bytes, so only its first 32 bytes are signed; pass it on BOTH sides.
    --rounds (hpks-stern, hpks-ring, nl-zkboo, nl-zkbpp) defaults to 219 in all
    four CLIs, the 128-bit Fiat-Shamir count.
    hpks-wots / hpks-xmss keep one-time-use / leaf-index state in a <keyfile>.idx
    sidecar; reusing a WOTS key or an XMSS leaf breaks the signature.
  verify --algo {sign algos + hpks-t} --pubkey FILE [--ring ...] --in FILE --sig FILE
         [--digest {hfscx-256,none}] [--min-rounds N]
    The round count travels in the artifact, so the verifier sets a floor:
    hpks-stern, hpks-ring, nl-zkboo and nl-zkbpp artifacts declaring fewer than
    --min-rounds (default 219) are refused (TODO #364, v15.0.0).
  threshold-commit --key FILE --commit-out FILE --nonce-out FILE
  threshold-aggregate --commits FILE... --in FILE --out FILE [--digest {hfscx-256,none}]
  threshold-respond --key FILE --commits FILE... --aggregate FILE --nonce FILE --out FILE
  threshold-combine --aggregate FILE --partials FILE... --out FILE
    threshold-* take 256-bit hpks/hpks-nl keys only; a narrower one is refused at commit
    (TODO #388).
    Since TODO #270 (v6.4.0) all four CLIs accept BOTH spellings of these list
    flags with BOTH syntaxes: --commits a b, --commit a --commit b, --commits a
    --commits b and --commit a b are equivalent (likewise --partials/--partial).
    Python and Java took only the plural and C and Go only the singular until
    then, so the capability was in all four under two names and a documented
    command line did not port.  MIXING the two names in one invocation is
    refused: the list order is consensus-critical (threshold-respond must see the
    order threshold-aggregate did), so there is no defensible interleaving.
  threshold-verify --sig FILE --in FILE [--digest {hfscx-256,none}]
    (HPKS-T 4-phase flow: commit -> aggregate -> respond -> combine, then verify.
     threshold-verify is a directly-invokable top-level subcommand in GO ONLY.
     C dispatches `verify` and delegates internally to cmd_threshold_verify;
     Python and Java expose the check only via `verify --algo hpks-t`.  Same
     operation and same PEM in all four -- one extra entry point in Go.
     Corrected by TODO #267's CLI-surface matrix, which had said "C and Go".)
  encfile/decfile --algo hske-nla1 --key FILE --in FILE --out FILE   (streaming, .hkx)
  dgst --algo {hfscx-256,hfscx-256-ds} --in FILE [--out FILE]
  rand [--seed FILE|--state FILE] [--personalization STR] [--reseed FILE]
       --bytes N [--hex] [--out FILE]
    All four CLIs since TODO #269 (v6.3.0); Java shipped the HDRBG primitive from
    the start and the subcommand only now.  --state is both the resume source and
    the checkpoint destination, and the HERRADURA HDRBG STATE PEM is byte-identical
    across all four writers.
  fpe/twk --key FILE (--encrypt|--decrypt) [--v3] --in FILE --out FILE [--context STR | --sector N --bidx N]
    --v3 selects the NL-FSCX v3 round and its own subkey domain (tags 0x22/0x23
    against v2's 0x20/0x21), so a --v3 artifact does not decrypt without --v3 —
    and, being an unauthenticated permutation, it fails by returning wrong bytes
    rather than an error.  ALL FOUR CLIs, Java included: TODO #260 added Java's
    fpe and twk in v5.3.6, and this line went on saying it shipped neither until
    TODO #269 re-checked it (v6.3.0).
    twk's --sector is decimal 0..2^64-1 and --bidx decimal 0..2^32-1; every CLI
    refuses any other value by name rather than wrapping it onto another block's
    tweak (TODO #375).
    --in must be exactly 32 bytes in every CLI, both modes, with or without --v3;
    longer input used to be cut to 32 and shorter zero-padded (on the left in Go
    only).  Exactly one of --encrypt / --decrypt (TODO #377).
  oprf-blind --in FILE [--bits 32|64|128|256] --out FILE
  oprf-eval --key FILE --in FILE --out FILE
  oprf-unblind --state FILE --eval FILE --out FILE
    --bits (default 256) is the GF(2^n) width and must be the server key's n: the
    CLIENT STATE and EVALUATION PEMs carry n, and oprf-eval / oprf-unblind refuse a
    pair from two widths by name.  Below 256 bits H(x) is the high n bits of
    HFSCX-256(x).  pake-register / pake-demo run at the key's n (TODO #385).
  pake-register --key FILE [--username U] [--password P | --password-file F] --out FILE
  pake-demo --key FILE [--username U] [--password P | --password-file F]
    --username exists in Python and Java only; it is a lookup label, not bound into the
    record, so C and Go records are byte-comparable (spec cli_surface_gaps).
    pake-register needs a non-empty --password in every CLI (Python alone may prompt
    for it, on a terminal); pake-demo defaults to "demo-password" but refuses ''
    (TODO #376).
  cred-issue --our FILE --in FILE [--rounds N] --out FILE
  cred-prove --in FILE [--msg STR] [--rounds N] --out FILE
  cred-verify --proof FILE --pubkey FILE [--msg STR] [--cred FILE --issuer FILE]
              [--min-rounds N]
    Refuses a proof or credential declaring fewer than --min-rounds (default 219)
    rounds (TODO #364).  See docs/TUTORIAL.md for the full HCRED flow.

## Language-specific notes for integrators
- C: `#include "herradura.h"` directly; no separate compilation unit needed.
- Go: import "herradurakex/herradura" (add a `replace` directive if vendoring outside
  this module, mirroring HerraduraCli/go.mod).
- Python: the suite/CLI filenames contain spaces — use importlib.util.spec_from_file_location,
  not a normal `import` statement (see HerraduraCli/primitives.py).
- Cross-language interop is verified by CliTest/test_*_interop.sh — consult those scripts
  for concrete byte-compatible PEM examples if debugging wire-format issues.
